scenes.heading: Development Tools
scenes.narration: Env Setup. Development Tools. In this video we review 8 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: Which Java version is recommended for local AEM development?
scenes.heading: Java JDK 21
scenes.body: Java JDK 21 is the recommended version for AEM development. AEM is a Java application, so the correct JDK must be installed before starting local development.

scenes.question: What command verifies that Java is correctly installed on your system?
scenes.heading: java -version
scenes.body: After installing Java JDK, you verify the installation with the command `java -version`. This prints the installed JDK version to confirm it is correctly set up.

scenes.question: What is the build tool used for all AEM projects?
scenes.heading: Apache Maven
scenes.body: Apache Maven is the build tool for all AEM projects. It compiles Java code, runs tests, and packages the code into OSGi bundles and content packages for deployment.

scenes.question: What command verifies that Apache Maven is correctly installed?
scenes.heading: mvn -v
scenes.body: You verify Maven is installed correctly with `mvn -v`, which prints the Maven version, Java version, and OS information. This confirms the Maven installation is working.

scenes.question: Why is Node.js required in the AEM local development environment?
scenes.heading: For front-end tooling and the Adobe I/O CLI
scenes.body: Node.js is required for front-end tooling (like webpack, Sass compilation) and for the Adobe I/O CLI (`aio`), which is installed as a global npm package. It is not used to run AEM itself.

scenes.question: What command verifies that Node.js is correctly installed?
scenes.heading: node --version
scenes.body: After installing Node.js, you verify it with `node --version`, which prints the installed Node.js version number. This confirms Node.js is available in your PATH.

scenes.question: Which of the following is one of the four core tools required for local AEM development?
scenes.heading: Git — for source control
scenes.body: The four core tools required for local AEM development are: Java JDK 21, Node.js, Apache Maven, and Git. Git is used for source control of the AEM project.

scenes.question: What is the recommended practice after installing each development tool for AEM?
scenes.heading: Verify the installation with a version command
scenes.body: After installing each tool (Java, Maven, Node.js, Git), you should always verify with a version command: `java -version`, `mvn -v`, `node --version`, and `git --version`. This confirms the tool is installed and on the PATH.
